title: Supervised deep learning for efficient cryo-EM image alignment in drug discovery with cryoPARES
desc: Cryo-Electron Microscopy (cryo-EM) is a pivotal tool for determining 3D structures of biological macromolecules. Current workflows are computationally demanding and require manual intervention, creating bottlenecks for high-throughput applications like structure-based drug discovery. In such contexts, where all protein samples can be assumed to be equivalent at resolutions relevant for image alignment, information about particle poses from previous refinements could be reused. Existing methods, however, ignore this prior knowledge, aligning each dataset from scratch. We present cryoPARES, a deep learning pose estimation method trained on pre-aligned datasets. Our method not only provides accurate angular predictions significantly faster than traditional approaches but also introduces automated particle pruning capabilities that eliminate manual intervention. Together with its single-pass operation, these features enable near real-time reconstructions that provide feedback during data acquisition. We demonstrate cryoPARES’s effectiveness through rapid structural determination of seven ligand-bound complexes across four distinct protein targets. We also release three fragment-bound cryo-EM datasets.

title: Reclaiming the Narrative: Why Humanism and Narratology Must Counter the Rise of Algorithmic Medicine.
source: PubMed · Journal of general internal medicine
desc: [Journal of general internal medicine] As artificial intelligence (AI) promises diagnostic precision approaching human expertise, medicine faces a profound paradox: expanding technological capabilities risk eroding the human encounter between caregiver and patient. The Age of Reason in medicine has privileged quantifiable, systematized knowledge validated through randomized controlled trials, yet this epistemological dominance threatens to hollow out medicine's humanistic core. While algorithms excel at pattern recognition and prediction, they cannot grapple with ambiguity, uncertainty, or the irreducible complexity of human suffering. AI deployment risks creating an "AI trust gap" and automation bias among clinicians. Narrative medicine offers an essential counterweight, defining illness as a meaningful disruption of a person's life story rather than merely a departure from physiological norms. Empirical evidence demonstrates that narrative medicine training improves empathy, communication skills, and clinical outcomes. This perspective argues for mandatory, longitudinal narrative medicine curricula and institutional reforms that recognize humanistic practice as a core professional competency, ensuring AI serves rather than obscures medicine's irreducible humanity.

title: Learning spatial cellular state through 3D reconstruction of the cell
desc: Subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics localizes individual RNA transcripts within cells with high-precision. Existing methods for identifying spatially organized cell populations rely on cellular niches defined by neighboring cells, leaving open whether such populations can be identified from individual-cell representations alone. Moreover, representations that jointly capture transcript identity and three-dimensional (3D) spatial organization have not been systematically learned or biologically evaluated. Here we present a representation learning framework that models each cell as a gene-annotated point cloud of transcripts and trains a rotation-equivariant neural network to reconstruct 3D cell shape, yielding spatially informed transcript embeddings. We further aggregate these embeddings into a cell-state representation that summarizes transcript-level spatial patterns. Our framework outperforms existing point-cloud-based 3D reconstruction methods on cell-shape reconstruction. In MERFISH human uterine cancer, combining the learned embeddings with gene expression improved prediction of CD45RO protein intensity over both gene expression alone and niche-based embeddings. Applied to MERFISH human liver cancer and Xenium human lung datasets, our framework identified distinct spatial patterns between cell populations, including spatially organized subpopulations marked by disease-associated gene expression and patterns associated with pathological tissue structures. Together, these results show that learning transcript representations through 3D cell reconstruction provides a novel approach to capture cell-state heterogeneity and biologically relevant spatial organization in subcellular spatial transcriptomics.

Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic health age using wearables and blood biomarkers
desc: Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents a growing public health crisis, yet its subclinical heterogeneity remains underexplored. Early detection of physiological deviation is critical for preventing irreversible organ damage. Here, we characterize the prevalence and interplay of CKM impairment in a US cohort (WEAR-ME study, N = 819 participants) by integrating continuous wearable data with clinical biomarkers. We assessed cardiovascular, kidney via clinical biomarkers, namely Chol/HDL, eGFR, as well as metabolic health risk through Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR). We show that while metabolic and cardiovascular disruptions are significantly associated (r = 0.26, p < 0.001), early-stage kidney impairment manifests independently. Utilizing a normalized deviance score, we identified significant health impairments in 29.0% of the cohort. Cardiovascular deviation was the most prevalent singular phenotype (13.3%), followed by metabolic (9.1%) and renal (6.25%) deviations, with dual metabolic-cardiovascular impairment occurring in only 2.2% of participants. These findings suggest that high system-specific deviance may serve as an indicator for accelerated physiological aging within the respective organ system. Furthermore, step count, active zone minutes, and resting heart rate were identified as the key wearable predictors of cardiovascular and metabolic decline. Leveraging wearables metrics and blood biomarkers, we developed a CKM Health Age model that tracks physiological health, aligning with established clinical standards (Metabolic syndrome severity and modified AHA Life’s Essential 8) and user-reported overall health. These findings underscore the necessity of a multi-system subtyping approach, demonstrating that wearable-derived phenotypes and routine blood biomarkers can facilitate the early, targeted interventions required to manage the complex landscape of CKM syndrome.

title: Bridging the Gender Gap in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Machine Learning Approach to Screening Women for Moderate-to-Severe Disease.
source: PubMed · Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
desc: [Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases] Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) can lead to severe complications if left untreated. Several challenges hinder OSA identification in females, resulting in underdiagnosis and undertreatment in this population. This study aimed to develop a machine learning (ML) approach specifically tailored to screen women for moderate-to-severe OSA. A retrospective study was conducted using clinical records of 1,210 women who underwent polysomnography at our institution. Collected data included demographics, body metrics, nocturnal oxygen saturation levels, medical conditions, medications, laboratory measurements, and polysomnography results. Four ML algorithms were employed to classify participants into moderate-to-severe and none-to-mild OSA groups. Due to the high missingness of laboratory values in the whole cohort, two sets of models were developed: one utilizing all subjects but excluding lab tests, and another restricted to a subgroup of 383 participants that additionally incorporated hemoglobin and lipid profile alongside the other features. Without laboratory measurements, the best-performing model was adaptive boosting, which achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and accuracy of 0.811 and 76.03%, respectively. When lab tests were included, gradient boosting machine outperformed its competitors, with the above metrics reaching 0.872 and 84.42%, respectively. The promising performance of our approach underlines the potential of artificial intelligence in refining screening strategies for OSA in women. Nadir oxygen saturation during sleep emerged as a particularly strong predictor, reinforcing the central role of nocturnal hypoxemia in OSA risk stratification. Future research should focus on incorporating broader clinical inputs and using larger, diverse datasets to develop a highly accurate, robust model that meets clinical standards and is suitable for real-world implementation.

title: Accurate and interpretable protein complex stoichiometry prediction through agentic AI with StoiAgent
desc: Accurate protein complex structure modeling requires knowledge of complex stoichiometry, yet the copy numbers of individual subunits are often unknown. Consequently, predicting protein complex stoichiometry has emerged as a major challenge in recent years. Here, we present StoiAgent, a large language model (LLM)-powered AI agent that automates the retrieval and integration of sequence, structural, and literature evidence to predict stoichiometry while preserving interpretable reasoning traces (chain of thoughts) of its evidence assessment and ranking decision. An open-weight LLM model, Qwen3.6-27B, is used by StoiAgent as the LLM backbone to combine sequences, structural templates, AlphaFold3 structure predictions, and literature evidence, and perform stoichiometry candidate generation and ranking. On 56 CASP17 protein complex targets, it achieves top-1 accuracy of 75.0%, which represents a 23.2 percentage-point improvement over PreStoi with AlphaFold3 ranking (51.8%) and matches the top-1 accuracy of StoPred. Moreover, StoiAgent has a higher top-3 and top-5 accuracy than StoPred (85.7% versus 80.4% and 87.5% versus 85.7%, respectively). Furthermore, it outperforms general-purpose frontier LLMs, including ChatGPT and Gemini, in stoichiometry prediction. Case studies further illustrate how StoiAgent evaluates competing assembly hypotheses by integrating complementary evidence, with recorded reasoning traces documenting its decision-making process. Overall, StoiAgent demonstrates the potential of LLM-powered AI agents to improve protein complex stoichiometry prediction through the automated integration of diverse sources of evidence while providing interpretable explanations to guide downstream structure modeling.

Network meta-analysis of digital interventions for fibromyalgia
desc: This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated digital interventions for function, pain, and depression in adults with fibromyalgia. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched up to 1 February 2026. Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed using RoB 2.0 and Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA). Twenty-three randomized controlled trials involving 1540 participants were included. Random-effects network meta-analysis showed that digital psychological-behavioral interventions (DPI) and tele-rehabilitation guidance (TRG) significantly reduced pain versus waitlist (WL) or treatment-as-usual (TAU) controls (DPI: SMD: −1.25, 95% CI: −2.01 to −0.48, moderate certainty of evidence; TRG: SMD: −1.15, 95% CI: −1.86 to −0.43, low certainty of evidence). No significant overall effects were observed for fibromyalgia impact or depression. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested different patterns across age and intervention-duration strata, but effect modification was not formally tested. Heterogeneity and imprecision limit interpretation. Larger standardized trials are needed to clarify treatment modifiers and inform personalized care.

title: Overview of In Silico Methods in Microbiome Studies.
source: PubMed · Advances in experimental medicine and biology
desc: [Advances in experimental medicine and biology] The recent advances in in-silico platforms have paved a way in rapid evolving of bioinformatics-based microbiome platforms such as multiomics techniques like amplicon sequencing or metagenomic, metatranscriptomics datasets. Advances in silico approach in such platforms have created vast datasets which provide effective relevant biological interpretations. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of various computational software or packages applied for microbiome studies. Such frameworks highlight taxonomic profiling of microbial communities, microbes-host interaction, their functional annotations and disease relevance. Various established pipelines use machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithmic platforms which are discussed, putting an emphasizes on microbial profiling of samples, their comparative performance with preclinical/clinical evidences. Choice of relevant packages or collective pipelines significantly influence quantitative interpretation of microbiome datasets; the core biological inferences showed consistency yet increase in development of standard pipelines with precision is an unwaivable requirement for improving in silico dependent microbiome studies. The present study further explores applications and challenges of in silico platforms in relation to microbiome and their limited mechanistic studies. Future perspectives emphasize in development of microbial cloud-based pipelines, integrative multiomics and benchmarking in-silico platforms. Overall, this work highlights the present in silico platforms for microbiome studies of predictive modeling with mechanistic approach, shifting a focus towards an improved and better platforms from descriptive to predictive translational microbiome modeling.

title: BI-SCUDO Regression - A novel algorithm to infer clinical variables from omics datasets
desc: Regression analysis of high-throughput omics data is often made difficult by noise, batch effects, and the loss of information resulting from the discretization of continuous variables. Existing machine learning algorithms often struggle to extract stable biological signals under these heterogeneous conditions. We introduce BI-SCUDO Regression, a rank-based regression framework designed for omics data analysis. By leveraging within-sample rankings and network-based predictions, BI-SCUDO Regression bypasses the need for complex normalization and provides robust, interpretable results. In synthetic benchmarks, BI-SCUDO Regression demonstrated strong resilience to noise, maintaining predictive and feature-selection stability under conditions in which standard models exhibited performance degradation. When applied to cohorts from TCGA datasets, BI-SCUDO Regression consistently outperformed LASSO, Random Forest Regression, and XGBoost in predicting survival, with an average increase in Ratio of Performance to Deviation ranging from 43% to 86%, depending on the comparator. Furthermore, the algorithm consistently identified parsimonious, statistically significant, and biologically relevant biomarkers, with enrichment for cancer-related terms across all stage stratifications. Although BI-SCUDO Regression incurs higher training times due to its genetic optimization strategy, it offers a robust and interpretable approach to outcome prediction and biomarker discovery, with potential applications in precision medicine, where noisy data compromise the performance of conventional regression methods.

Bidirectional multi-scale implicit neural representation network for topology-aware lung 4D-CT registration.
source: PubMed · Physics in medicine and biology
desc: [Physics in medicine and biology] Objective.Precise lung 4D-CT registration is extremely challenging due to large respiratory excursions. To capture such large-magnitude motion, existing deep learning methods typically adopt a unidirectional coarse-to-fine cascade strategy, which is vulnerable to error propagation because uncorrected coarse-level misalignments degrade subsequent finer-scale stages and often lead to spatially inconsistent deformations. While implicit neural representations (INRs) support continuous coordinate-based deformation modeling, traditional instance-specific INRs lack clinical efficiency and struggle to converge on global large deformations because of the absence of multi-scale semantic guidance. This study aims to bridge these gaps by developing a bidirectional multi-scale INR network that jointly handles large deformation modeling and localized structural fidelity.Approach.We propose a bidirectional multi-scale INR network. First, a generalized conditional INR framework is introduced to enable continuous deformation modeling without the need for retraining. Crucially, a bidirectional feature feedback mechanism built upon Swin Transformer injects high-level semantic priors into low-resolution streams, correcting coarse-level biases through top-down interaction. Furthermore, an anatomy-aware structural constraint is incorporated to promote anatomical consistency and local boundary alignment.Main results.Under the within-subject phase-held-out DIR-Lab protocol, the proposed method achieved a mean TRE of 1.28 mm and a folding rate of 0.0090%. A leave-one-case-out evaluation assessed subject-independent generalization, yielding a mean TRE of 1.53 mm and a folding rate of 0.0195%. On the independent POPI dataset, the method achieved a mean TRE of 1.84 mm and a folding rate of 0.0806%, demonstrating competitive cross-center performance. Inference took 0.33 s per case.Significance.The proposed framework effectively combines continuous coordinate modeling with deep learning efficiency, overcoming error propagation inherent in discrete coarse-to-fine strategies and preserving both global deformation consistency and local anatomical precision. Its sub-second inference and performance under leave-one-case-out and independent external testing support its potential for efficient image-guided radiation therapy workflows.

title: GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes from histology to map senescence across aging and disease
desc: Spatial omics has generated measurements at unprecedented scale, yet computational approaches remain largely confined to individual modalities and 2D representations. Here we assemble ImageOmicsNet-300M, a corpus of 300 million single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiles, including 24.9 million H&E-predicted virtual spatial transcriptomics profiles, and 4,623 H&E sections. Of these H&E sections, we generated 1,782 from aging mouse organs and serially sectioned human skin spanning five decades, with matched spatial transcriptomics and snRNA-seq. Building on this resource, we develop GenVinci, a multimodal tissue foundation model that reconstructs 3D tissue scenes from routine 2D histology. GenVinci predicts spatial gene expression from H&E with zero-shot generalization and maps senescence-associated states across 85.8 million cells, revealing cell-type-specific patterns and disease-associated remodeling. Integration with human genetics implicates suprabasal keratinocytes in atopic dermatitis and keratinocyte carcinomas, linked to higher and lower p16 and p21 expression, respectively. These findings establish GenVinci as a framework mapping senescence in 3D across scales.

Exploring clinician interpretability of AI decision support systems for surgical anatomy recognition.
desc: [Scientific reports] Artificial intelligence (AI) decision support systems for surgery hold promise but face barriers to adoption, particularly around the interpretability of their outputs. We conducted an international cross-sectional survey of 47 neurosurgeons to evaluate perspectives on literature-derived explanatory techniques for AI-generated anatomical segmentations, using endoscopic pituitary surgery as a high-risk exemplar. Participants ranked certainty scores, certainty maps, saliency maps, scene similarity scores, and nearest-neighbour illustrations, and rated them using a modified Explanation Satisfaction Scale alongside free-text feedback. Certainty-based techniques were consistently ranked and rated highest - valued for aligning with surgical decision-making by conveying confidence (via scores) and anatomical boundaries (via maps). Saliency- and similarity-based methods were judged less clinically relevant and better suited to educational settings. Therefore, certainty-based techniques appear most acceptable to surgeons for improving the interpretability of AI-assisted anatomical navigation systems, though their impact on trust calibration and performance requires prospective evaluation across surgical domains. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-74953-y.

title: BiomedCAT: Biomedical Context Analysis Tool for Supporting Mechanistic Hypothesis Generation via User-defined Contextual Subgraph Extraction
desc: Researchers formulate mechanistic hypotheses in slides and figures long before they write them as text, yet knowledge-graph (KG) tools expect a query in the vocabulary of the graph. We present BiomedCAT, an open-source workflow that turns biomedical slides into a subgraph of the RTX-KG2c knowledge graph shaped by the user's research profile, on a laptop and without sending the documents out. A small vision-language model describes each slide; a 4-billion-parameter agent types the terms into the classes of the Biolink model; an existence gate removes invented entities; identifiers are retrieved from Translator services or from a local table and selected, never generated, by a judge model; and a profile-weighted two-hop expansion builds the context graph. On a synthetic Biolink typing benchmark whose labels were audited by an expert, the local agent reaches 0.71 accuracy on 517 non-ambiguous mentions, 4 points below Claude Opus 5 (0.75), level with DeepSeek-V4-Flash (0.69) and above open-weight models of 24 and 31 billion parameters; the audit also showed that 55% of the generated labels were wrong or ambiguous. On expert-annotated slide decks, the reading stage recovers 81 to 94% of the explicit terms of the English deck, less on French decks, and linking assigns the expert identifier to 65% of the found terms online and 26% in the fully local mode. A one-slide run takes 33 to 42 minutes, with peaks of 9.8~GB of system RAM above idle and 5.3~GB of GPU memory. In a facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) case, three slides that each draw one pathway from DUX4 at a different biological scale give graphs that overlap by 7 to 15% of their nodes, each recovering its own pathway's expected nodes, and expose sourced paths from DUX4, such as a DUX4--HMGB1 interaction from IntAct. Of 21 compounds tested in FSHD, seven, including every agent that targets DUX4, are absent from RTX-KG2c, which bounds what a graph-based approach can propose. BiomedCAT lets a researcher set a working hypothesis against curated knowledge, with every edge traceable to its source.

Moving Toward Clinical Cardiac Magnetic Resonance: Full Integration of Imaging Data into Patient Care Pathways.
desc: [Heart failure clinics] Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) provides the greatest clinical value when performed to answer a specific clinical question rather than as a stand-alone imaging test. The significance of CMR findings depends on integration with the patient's clinical history, Electrocardiogram , laboratory data, and other imaging results. In heart failure, clinical CMR supports etiologic diagnosis, phenotyping, risk stratification, therapeutic decisions, and selected follow-up. title: scUNVEIL: Learning scRNA-seq Cell Embeddings Through Measurement Enrichment
desc: Large-scale pretraining can improve scRNA-seq representations through measurement enrichment: estimating what the same measurement would reveal at greater UMI depth under the same measurement process. We introduce scUNVEIL, a self-supervised model trained through next-UMI prediction. We show that the Bayes-optimal next-UMI predictor is the posterior mean of the transcriptome composition that arbitrarily deep sequencing would reveal. Because UMI identities are exchangeable conditional on transcriptome composition, scUNVEIL operates directly on count vectors using a residual multilayer perceptron, without attention over gene tokens. The measurement-enriched transcriptome composition is predicted from a single low-dimensional hidden state, which therefore serves naturally as the cell embedding. The same model provides both reusable cell representations and measurement-enriched gene-expression estimates. scUNVEIL was pretrained without labels or auxiliary metadata on approximately 92 million human cells spanning diverse tissues. Under linear evaluation on fine-grained cell-type annotation, its zero-shot representations achieved the best performance among the evaluated methods, while providing over 1000-fold faster inference than the strongest evaluated transformer-based foundation model and matching that model's predictive performance using 88% fewer input UMIs per cell. Further evaluations show that these representations improve prediction of tumor reactivity, mitochondrial membrane potential, cell morphology, and lineage-associated treatment outcomes.

Sustainable Functional Food Packaging: From Laboratory Innovation to Industrial Translation Through Scalability, Techno-Economic Screening, and AI-Enabled Strategies.
source: PubMed · Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety
desc: [Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety] Sustainable functional food packaging offers opportunities to improve food safety, extend shelf life, and reduce dependence on conventional petroleum-based packaging. However, a persistent gap remains between laboratory-scale innovations and industrial implementation because functional performance is often prioritized over scalability, processing stability, cost, and regulatory readiness. This review critically evaluates the industrial translation of sustainable functional packaging by comparing conventional and emerging fabrication technologies in terms of production throughput, processing conditions, bioactive stability, energy demand, equipment requirements, and technology readiness levels (TRLs). Extrusion and film blowing offer the highest nominal throughput (50-500+ kg/h; indicative TRL 8-9 depending on the functional packaging format), while printing and coating provide approximately 10-100 kg/h (TRL 7-9). In contrast, solvent casting, freeze-drying, electrospinning, and 3D printing remain constrained by batch operation, energy demand, low throughput, or process complexity. Particular attention is given to techno-economic screening considerations, industrial case studies, food-contact regulations, migration and safety assessment, and the trade-offs between functionality and manufacturing feasibility. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are further considered as potentially enabling tools for formulation optimization, process control, quality prediction, scale-up support, and regulatory assessment, although their industrial application remains limited by data availability, model validation, and regulatory acceptance. The review identifies industrially informed material design, scalable encapsulation, hybrid processing, data-driven manufacturing, and circular-economy integration as key priorities for closing the laboratory-to-market gap.

title: DRAFT: graph-recurrent learning of dynamic gene regulatory networks along single-cell multi-omics trajectories
desc: Single-cell multi-omics data offer an opportunity to resolve how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are rewired during cell-fate transitions, but most existing methods infer static snapshots, ignore temporal dependencies or assume linear regulation. Here we present DRAFT, a deep learning framework that combines graph attention with recurrent temporal memory to infer dynamic GRNs from time-resolved single-cell multi-omics data. On simulated data, DRAFT outperforms existing methods in accuracy and temporal smoothness. In mouse cellular reprogramming and Drosophila adult spermatogenesis, it recovers interactions supported by independent ChIP-seq, perturbation and Hi-C data, together with known stage-specific regulators. By inferring regulatory activity from dynamic network structure rather than expression alone, DRAFT identifies regulators whose activity precedes their transcriptional peak, including the candidate early germline regulator Mondo. Germline-specific Mondo knockdown alters germline stem cell number and expression of the predicted targets kuz and mamo. DRAFT also enables nonlinear alignment of co-developing lineages and reveals stage-specific cell-cell communication.

ANCHOR: AI-NGS consensus hierarchy for optimized refinement of high-affinity binders from affinity maturation.
desc: [Briefings in bioinformatics] Affinity maturation for the systematic discovery of high-affinity protein reagents remains a major challenge in display-based protein engineering, largely because phenotypic enrichment frequently fails to correlate with true binding affinity. To improve candidate identification, we developed ANCHOR, an artificial intelligence (AI) and next-generation sequencing (NGS) consensus hierarchy for optimized refinement that implements a score-decoupled, two-stage strategy. Enrichment-trained classifier and regression models are used to construct a candidate pool, from which group-specific consensus sequences are subsequently derived without ranking candidates solely by individual model scores. Using the phosphotyrosine-binding Fyn SH2 domain as a model system, the two models achieved strong performance on untouched independent test sets (classification area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) = 0.974; regression Pearson's r = 0.870). By leveraging a biopanning-guided filter, ANCHOR reduced the searchable sequence space by approximately four orders of magnitude while maintaining a ~90% overlap with exhaustive screening and retained 297 enrichment-predicted variants. These variants were grouped by residue identity at the least-conserved position (P4) and consensus sequences were derived within each group. Among the 16 evaluable consensus variants, 9 (56%) matched or exceeded the affinity of TrM, a previously established 100-fold-improved superbinder, with several showing a two-fold further improvement. Exploratory analyses using a structural proxy indicated robustness to parameter choices and a higher observed hit rate for ANCHOR than for the evaluated alternatives. Application to a public anti-HER2 scFv yeast-display NGS dataset demonstrated computational portability across datasets and library designs. Collectively, ANCHOR provides a practical framework for prioritizing affinity-maturation candidates from display-derived NGS data.

title: GENECraft: A Function- and Prior-Constrained Discrete Dynamical System for Controllable Regulatory DNA Design
desc: Designing regulatory DNA requires reconciling two complementary modeling paradigms: genomic language models (gLMs) capture evolutionary syntax without guaranteeing targeted regulatory activity, whereas sequence-to-function predictors provide explicit functional supervision without enforcing native-like sequence plausibility. We introduce GENECraft, a training-free Function- and Prior-Constrained Discrete Dynamical System (FP-DDS) that couples a genomic language model (Carbon) and a functional oracle (AlphaGenome) during inference-time optimization to balance predicted regulatory activity and consistency with genomic sequence priors. GENECraft evolves continuous latent nucleotide logits while evaluating strictly decoded discrete DNA sequences under a time-dependent composite vector field that fuses normalized functional utility, bidirectional contextual prior guidance, and compositional quality penalties, followed by feasibility-first trajectory readout. Across 2,185 loci spanning promoters, multi-constraint enhancers, and 18 transcription factors (TFs), GENECraft achieves full-joint success rates of 62.70%, 65.23%, and 94.56% (macro-averaged), substantially outperforming seven optimization, evolutionary, and generative baselines (which reach at most 2.15% on enhancers). In matched 336-locus ablations, in-loop Carbon guidance reduces native-relative dinucleotide divergence by 7.8--11.5%, enhancer context sensitivity by 10.5%, and TF mutation sensitivity by 11.0%, establishing FP-DDS as a principled framework for controllable regulatory DNA design.

title: Beyond animal testing: integrated AI-PBPK-MPS framework for human-relevant toxicology.
desc: [Critical reviews in toxicology] NAMs are revolutionizing safety assessment and bridging the substantial disconnect between traditional animal toxicology studies and human exposure within the pharmaceutical industry. AI predictive toxicology uses graph neural networks, deep learning, explainable AI, PBPK, and IVIVE modeling for human-dose predictions, and micro-physiological and organ-on-a-chip systems that replicate specific physiological states. The development of NAMs has been applied to FDA initiatives, such as the Predictive Toxicology Roadmap, ISTAND MIDD, and CiPA, to demonstrate how integrated NAM systems optimized at early drug development stages provide valuable information on mechanistic toxicities related to humans and accelerate drug development. AI-QSAR models, PBPK simulations, and organ-on-a-chip technologies are increasingly integrated with discovery and early-stage preclinical workflows in different sectors. Standardization and reproducibility across platforms, transparency of AI models, multiomics integration, and global regulator convergence are required to improve the power of AI. This review is the first to provide a unified mechanistic synthesis of all three pillars of NAMs, AI-based predictive toxicology, PBPK-IVIVE modeling, and microphysiological systems (MPS), while earlier reviews covered them independently. We suggest a cyclical NAM ecosystem in which AI predictions seek translation to human pharmacokinetics, with iterative mechanistic validation via MPS, solving current challenges of translation from animals to humans. This review is distinct from others in that it presents NAM technologies as an integrated, human-relevant system rather than disparate technologies, and thus offers regulators a roadmap.

title: Flux Transformer learns intracellular metabolic fluxes from isotope labeling and measured reaction rates
desc: Cells convert incoming nutrients into energy and biomass via metabolic fluxes. Quantifying these fluxes involves feeding cells isotope-labeled nutrients, quantifying metabolite labeling patterns, and inverting the labeling data to retrieve the underlying flux distribution. Traditional metabolic flux analysis (MFA) is both computationally expensive and frequently requires manual refinement of the cost function to obtain plausible results. For this reason, MFA has remained inaccessible to non-experts. Here we present Flux Transformer, an AI model that uses reaction-specific attention to integrate isotope-labeling data with available reaction-rate measurements, reconstructing mass-balanced steady-state fluxes. The model is trained on simulated data with added noise and identifies the underlying fluxes from these data more effectively than traditional MFA. Provided experimental data from wild-type and mutant bacteria, yeast, plants, and mammalian T cells, it efficiently and accurately recovers expert-curated MFA fluxes. By making flux analysis accessible, Flux Transformer is poised to accelerate metabolic research and engineering.

title: An end-to-end residual convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold Network framework for robust gait phase recognition from surface EMG.
source: PubMed · Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
desc: [Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering] Accurate recognition of gait phases from surface electromyography (sEMG) signals is essential for intelligent prosthetics, exoskeletons, and rehabilitation. This study proposes a residual convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold network (RCKAN) that integrates convolutional feature encoding, ridge-regularized nonlinear mapping, and residual learning for five-phase gait classification. Experimental results on data from 40 healthy subjects demonstrate that RCKAN achieves state-of-the-art accuracy of 95.52%, surpassing conventional machine learning and advanced deep learning architectures. The model maintains strong performance in transitional phases such as heel strike and toe-off, confirming its robustness and potential for real-time gait analysis and assistive control applications.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Estimating Adjusted Treatment Effects in Presence of Nonspecific Treatment Responses: A Trial Simulation Study in Major Depressive Disorders.
desc: [Innovations in clinical neuroscience] Randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trials (RCTs) are the gold-standard approach for assessing treatment effect (TE), typically defined as baseline-corrected difference in clinical scores between active and placebo arms. Uncontrolled baseline variation in individuals' probability of exhibiting a nonspecific response to treatment (prob-NSRT) can introduce bias in the estimation of TEs, as conventional study designs and statistical methods generally fail to account for imbalances in such confounding factors. Recently, a novel methodology was proposed for assessing TE conditional to prob-NSRT estimated using artificial intelligence. The 1-(prob-NSRT) value was used as weight (propensity score weighted [PSW]) in a mixed model repeated measures (MMRM) analysis to assess TE by controlling the potential confounding effects of unbalanced baseline prob-NSRT distributions. Clinical trial simulations were conducted to explore multiple trial protocols (scenarios) and to identify alternative and more generalizable approaches for analyzing and reporting RCT results. The objective of this analysis was to compare the outcomes of PSW and the reference unadjusted analysis using simulated RCT data characterized by different baseline prob-NSRT distributions and to assess potential risk of inflating Type I/II errors. The simulations indicated that when using the unadjusted analysis, the risk of inflated Type I error increases with the increase of prob-NSRT and the risk of Type II error increases with the decrease of prob-NSRT. The PSW methodology achieved better control of baseline imbalance in nonspecific response distributions, yielding an estimated TE that was independent of prob-NSRT distributions. These findings provide convergent evidence highlighting the potential of PSW as the preferred approach for analyzing RCTs.

title: Invertible Gamut Mapping.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on image processing : a publication of the IEEE Signal Processing Society
desc: [IEEE transactions on image processing : a publication of the IEEE Signal Processing Society] Gamut mapping is a crucial component of the image signal processing (ISP) pipeline and color conversion between devices. Improper gamut mapping can introduce noticeable hue shifts and artifacts, resulting in poor visual quality. Although recent studies have significantly improved the fidelity of gamut extension through learning-based models and efficient metadata encoding schemes, the quality of gamut reduction and the intrinsic relationship between gamut reduction and extension have been largely overlooked. In this paper, we focus on developing deep learning-based approaches for gamut mapping that produce images with high color fidelity and perceptual quality for bidirectional conversion between wide gamut and small gamut. We propose an invertible framework that performs both gamut reduction and gamut extension within a single model. In the forward pass, the input wide-gamut image is decomposed into a clipped component and a residual component, which are jointly transformed into a small-gamut image and a latent variable. In the reverse pass, the small-gamut image and a Gaussian latent variable are used to reconstruct the wide-gamut image. To ensure that gamut reduction preserves hue and perceptual color similarity to the wide-gamut image, we introduce a self-supervised hue loss. We conduct experiments on three different gamut mapping scenarios: ProPhoto RGB to sRGB, BT.2020 to sRGB, and sRGB to a smaller "Toy" gamut. The proposed method outperforms previous metadata-free approaches in both color fidelity and perceptual quality across the evaluated gamut mapping scenarios.

title: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions.
desc: [Nature communications] Monitoring large-scale neuronal activity in deep brain circuits is crucial for understanding the principles of brain function. However, existing large-scale cellular-resolution imaging techniques are limited in imaging depth and cannot monitor activity in areas deeper than the cortex in the intact brain. To address this challenge, we developed a Large Imaging Field of view Three-photon (LIFT) microscope with a FOV of > 3 mm2. LIFT combines high-numerical-aperture optimized sampling, using a custom scanning module, with deep learning-based denoising, to enable population imaging in subcortical brain regions of mice and deep cortical regions of rats. We demonstrate calcium imaging in the intact mouse brain from more than 1500 cells across CA1, the surrounding white matter, and adjacent deep layers of the cortex, and show population imaging with high SNR at a depth of 1.2 mm in the rat cortex. The LIFT microscope offers versatility in imaging scale and rate and was built entirely from off-the-shelf components.

title: Physician AI disclosure, condition severity, and public trust in digital medicine
desc: Public trust is central to the implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital medicine, yet little is known about how patients respond to different forms of physician AI disclosure across clinical risk contexts. In a 5 × 2 factorial experiment in mainland China, 1574 adults were randomly assigned to physician profiles varying by AI use type and condition severity. Administrative AI was rated more favorably than diagnostic and therapeutic AI across physician perception and care-seeking intention outcomes. High-severity conditions amplified negative responses to therapeutic AI, whereas explicit non-AI disclosure was associated with greater appointment willingness under high severity. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that competence, trust, and empathy accounted for different disclosure-related response patterns. Main effects were directionally consistent in a supplementary offline community sample from Macao (n = 128). These findings suggest that AI disclosure in digital medicine should distinguish administrative from clinical uses and be calibrated to clinical severity, while highlighting the need for preregistered replication using behavioral outcomes.

title: Machine Learning Approaches to Biologic Therapy Response in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Review Article.
desc: [Sage open pathology] Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, remains a complex and heterogeneous condition with variable response to biologic therapies. Despite significant advances with anti-TNF agents, integrin inhibitors, and interleukin-12/23 blockers, treatment outcomes are limited by primary nonresponse, secondary loss of efficacy, immunogenicity, and substantial healthcare costs. The advent of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) algorithms, offers new opportunities to address these challenges by integrating diverse clinical, laboratory, imaging, histologic, genetic, and microbiome data. Recent studies demonstrate that AI-based models achieve high accuracy in predicting biologic response, remission, and adverse outcomes, outperforming conventional statistical approaches. AI has also shown promise in real-time endoscopic assessment, histologic grading, and forecasting disease progression, enabling earlier intervention and personalized therapy. However, current models are constrained by limited datasets, heterogeneity, lack of large-scale prospective validation, and concerns regarding interpretability, transparency, and patient privacy. Future efforts should prioritize multicenter trials, external validation, and ethical integration into clinical workflows. Collectively, AI-driven prediction of biologic therapy response represents a pivotal step toward precision medicine in IBD, with the potential to optimize therapeutic strategies, reduce ineffective treatment exposure, and improve patient outcomes.

title: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus
desc: Deep models often rely on spurious correlations that fail on underrepresented groups. Existing methods either correct human-specified bias attributes or infer unknown biases from the learned representation space. However, annotated attributes may differ from the shortcuts actually used by a model, while a single representation provides incomplete and potentially noisy evidence. Our key insight is that a bias obscured in one feature space may be clearer in another. In this work, we propose CHORD (Cross-view Harmonic Outlier Reversal for Debiasing), a multi-view framework that allows samples to "sing in chorus" across diverse representation spaces to achieve robust cross-view consensus. CHORD aggregates aggregates within-class partitions in each view, which is a proxy for specifying candidate biases, to debias the target representation and classifier without bias supervision. Experiments on seven benchmarks across vision, language, speech, and medical imaging show consistent improvements in worst-group accuracy. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/davelee-uestc/chord_debiasing_public .

title: TabBioMed: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Biomedical Tabular Learning
desc: Recent advances in machine learning have accelerated biomedical prediction, but evaluation on structured biomedical data remains fragmented, especially for datasets with high dimensionality, large sample size, missingness, and class imbalance. We introduce TabBioMed, a large-scale benchmark of 94 curated public biomedical tabular datasets spanning electronic health records, drug discovery, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, single-cell omics, and systems biology. TabBioMed unifies these datasets through a standardized, dataset-aware preprocessing and evaluation framework, enabling reproducible comparison across classification, regression, and multi-target tasks. We benchmark 23 models across classical baselines, gradient-boosted trees, neural tabular architectures, and tabular foundation models. Foundation models deliver the strongest family-level predictive performance. However, their gains are regime-dependent: tree-based models and tuned multilayer perceptrons remain highly competitive, often dominating under inference-time or training-cost constraints. Overall, TabBioMed shows that biomedical tabular learning is strongly context-dependent, with optimal model choice depending on data regime, task type, and computational budget. We release TabBioMed with curated datasets and splits, preprocessing code, baselines, and results, providing a reproducible benchmark for practical model selection and future methods development in biomedical machine learning, available at https://github.com/AI-sandbox/TabBioMed.

Imaging-based biological age gap and risk of mortality and incident diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis
desc: Artificial intelligence-derived imaging ageing clocks enable estimation of biological ageing from medical images. Yet meta-analytic quantification of the associations between imaging age gaps and both mortality and incident age-related diseases across multiple organs remains lacking. This study synthesised 40 eligible reports, of which 21 contributed to the meta-analysis. Meta-analyses showed that each 5-year increase in imaging age gap was associated with a higher hazard of all-cause mortality (HR 1.31, 95% CI 1.19–1.44), although heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 96.3%), with organ type and sample size contributing to heterogeneity. For cancer-specific mortality, the pooled HR was 1.06 (95% CI 0.96–1.18). Higher imaging age gaps were associated with incident dementia, stroke, heart failure, diabetes and hypertension, but not Parkinson’s disease. Imaging age gaps may support non-invasive risk stratification and long-term health management, but clinical translation requires standardisation, diverse external validation, interpretability, and evidence of clinical utility and equity.

title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.
desc: [Cornea] This study aims to elucidate the expanding role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the early diagnosis of corneal and ocular surface diseases. AI has the potential to enhance diagnostic precision, streamline clinical workflows, and facilitate disease detection before clinical manifestations become evident. A narrative literature review was conducted to assess the impact of AI and machine learning in corneal disease preclinical diagnosis. A comprehensive search in PubMed was performed using key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "machine learning," "deep learning," "corneal diseases," and "early diagnosis." Eligible studies were those published in English over the last decade that focused on AI-driven diagnostic approaches and prognostic modeling. Case reports, nonoriginal studies, and those with minimal AI integration were excluded. Data extraction emphasized AI methodologies, imaging techniques, diagnostic performance metrics, and clinical relevance. AI-powered machine learning models analyze vast imaging datasets, detecting subclinical abnormalities imperceptible to conventional diagnostic methods. This capability is particularly significant in early keratoconus detection, dystrophies, infectious keratitis, conjunctival neoplasia, and other corneal pathologies such as dry eye or Steven-Johnson disease, where subtle morphological changes precede clinically apparent disease. The integration of AI into corneal disease diagnostics and management could mark in the future a transformative shift in Ophthalmology, offering precision, efficiency, and scalability. By facilitating early disease detection and individualized patient assessments, AI minimizes diagnostic inconsistencies and accelerates clinical decision making. Continuous algorithm refinement and real-world validation are crucial to maximizing AI's clinical utility. To fully harness AI's potential, multidisciplinary collaboration among ophthalmologists, data scientists, and regulatory bodies is imperative to address standardization, ethical concerns, and implementation barriers. As AI-driven technologies continue to evolve, they will redefine the standard of care in corneal disease diagnosis, therapeutic precision, and patient outcomes.

title: Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents
desc: Clinicians reviewing a diagnostic work-up will ask what was considered at each step and why the assessment changed. Agents powered by free text can reach physician-level diagnostic accuracy, but their written reasoning does not always reflect the factors that went into the decision. Here, we present Decision2Care, a decision agent that works up the acutely ill patient without producing any text. A decision model assigns a probability to each permitted EHR action, and fixed rules carry out the most probable one. We evaluated Decision2Care on the records of 546 emergency admissions across 12 diseases. Decision2Care reached a diagnostic accuracy of 86.5%, compared with 86.1% for the MIRA-v2 agent, and required a median of 2.2 s per work-up, compared with 92-100 s. Each work-up tracked which options Decision2Care was considering at each step. In 10 of the 12 diseases, the differential diagnosis changed most at the test on which the guideline bases the diagnosis. Where Decision2Care was most confident after a single work-up, all but four of its diagnoses were correct (98.5%). We traced each of these four errors back to a single imaging report. Three of them were corrected when that report was removed. The same kind of decision was used to select the treatments, and Decision2Care's drug orders were judged guideline-adherent more often than MIRA-v2's. In emergency patients, its prediction of death was comparable to that of three intensivists on the same cases. In five of the eight intensive care cohorts, it exceeded the best of the three 24-h severity scores within 2-6 h of records. Our results show that decision agents can carry out clinical work-ups while recording the options, probabilities, and execution rules behind each action for audit.

title: AI Tracker: AWS launches new features for agentic AI tool
Artificial Intelligence in the Advancement of Mechanical Circulatory Support and Cardiac Care: A Systematic Review of Its Role and Potential.
desc: [Artificial organs] In recent years, there has been a notable surge in the ability of machines to perform complex and intelligent human-centered tasks, particularly within the domain of cardiovascular health. Rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms reflect the considerable potential for such analyses to meaningfully extend into translational device development and clinical usage of medical devices, especially mechanical circulatory support (MCS) therapies. Here, we investigate and report the applications, limitations, and strategies in which AI is currently being employed in MCS and the potential opportunities of AI approaches to advance the field of MCS. To effectively assess the scope and impact of AI in MCS, we conducted a systematic literature review. A comprehensive search of 4 recognized research databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, Ovid MEDLINE, and ProQuest) was performed using this Boolean string: "(Artificial Intelligence) AND (AI) AND (Mechanical Circulatory Support) AND (MCS) NOT (Heart Transplant) NOT (Cardiogenic Shock) NOT (Critical Care)." This strategy was designed to identify the application of AI in MCS only. Database search results were then screened by titles and abstracts, followed by full-text eligibility assessment and duplicate removal. Following these screening and eligibility steps, 30 of the 328 identified articles remained for inclusion. Most relevant publications covered two main subjects: the prediction and management of postoperative outcomes, and the development of personalized device-patient matching and timing. Across the reviewed studies, AI/ML models demonstrated promising performance in study-specific predictions of complications, recovery-related outcomes, and survival and were investigated as tools to support clinical decision-making. Barriers to broad implementation of AI include the necessity for sizable, high-quality datasets to achieve algorithm training benchmarks, the lack of organized and complete databases, such as INTERMACS, and limited computational resources. Emerging frontiers of MCS recognize the potential for AI and ML techniques to refine image recognition capabilities, diagnostic assessment, device placement, and post-implantation monitoring approaches in the future. AI-driven approaches demonstrate a promising convergence of computational power and clinical expertise, with the potential to support more personalized, efficient, and informed management of MCS patients.
